funding.supported_assets_note: Card Terms: a collateral-backed spending account — the Issuer 'establishes your credit limit' at 0% APR and spending is capped at the USD value of digital-asset collateral held 'in your custody within one or more smart contracts' (Issuer and Tria 'are not custodians'). Help centre: 'Your crypto stays in your control in your Tria wallet until it's used for a payment'; the card is loaded by depositing crypto from the Tria wallet or an external wallet on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Polygon, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Aptos, Tron or Solana (min $50 BTC / $10 other tokens; Avalanche not supported); conversion to local currency at payment via 'BestPath AVS'.

credit_terms.liquidation_risk: 0% APR on purchases (Important Disclosures effective 2025-10-31; US terms also 0% on balance transfers and cash advances). Collateral: '$100 USD' of collateral supports $100 of spending; limits 'can be reduced to $0' at any time. US terms: liquidation if a payment is not made within 21 days of the due date, or if collateral value drops below the charges and no collateral is added; collateral withdrawals need three business days' notice. The international terms mention no late, returned-payment or over-limit fees (all 'NA'). LTV for non-stable collateral not stated.

eligibility.nationality_restrictions_note: International Card Terms: the user attests to being 'not a United States citizen'; OFAC-sanctioned or blocked persons excluded.
eligibility.usage_note: No official country list on any page read. Card Terms: the card 'may not be available in all jurisdictions'; the help centre says the app's Country dropdown has 'over 200 supported regions' and names Australia, Canada, Germany, Hong Kong, the UAE, the UK and the US 'among many others' (KYC article), while the application article says unsupported countries 'will see a message indicating we are working to bring the card to your region'. Nigeria: card marketed by BANEX Microfinance Bank Limited (CBN-licensed). Country list must be confirmed per country in the app or from a published list.

kyc.stages_note: Order first, verify before activation: 'You can start your KYC once you have purchased your first Tria card'; personal details, government ID upload (retry with another document if rejected), live selfie matching the document, applicant physically present in the selected country of residence (camera + location permissions, VPN prohibited); 18+; one-time process. Verification provider not named ('an external link embedded within the app'). Proof of address not mentioned.

fees.conditions: 'Card issue: Virtual $25' (Important Disclosures). Whether the issue fee and the first annual fee are charged separately is not explained.
'Annual fee: Virtual $25'; 'Monthly fee: 0%'.

'USDC settlement/deposit: up to 1%' (Important Disclosures). Help centre markets 'zero deposit fees' / 'no Tria deposit fees on supported tokens' — see contradiction note; the dated terms govern and the maximum is modelled. Network gas: most chains gasless, Solana needs SOL, Tron needs TRX.

'Foreign exchange (FX): up to 3%' plus 'International transactions: up to 1%' (Important Disclosures). Help centre markets 'zero foreign exchange fees' (Tria FX fees waived, 'Visa foreign exchange fees may still apply') — see contradiction note; the dated terms govern and the maximum is modelled.

'ATM withdrawal: up to $2 + 3%'; balance inquiry up to $2; decline up to $2 (Important Disclosures). The help centre states ATM withdrawals are 'N/A' for the Lite (virtual) card — the fee applies to physical cards.

Active membership required; cap per user across cards; paid in USDT on Arbitrum in periodic batches (FAQ: quarterly, up to 90 days); refunds claw back cashback.

limits.note: No fixed limit: spending is capped by the USD value of posted collateral and 'can be reduced to $0' (Card Terms). Help centre: limits 'can be high (up to millions per day)'.

editorial.summary: Self-custodial Visa card from Tria: purchases run through a 0%-APR collateral-backed account (issuer Nimbus, LLC internationally, Third National in the US), with three paid annual tiers (US$25 virtual, US$109 plastic, US$250 metal) paying 1.5%, 4.5% or 6% cashback in USDT up to a monthly spend cap. The dated terms disclose FX up to 3% + 1%, deposit up to 1% and ATM US$2 + 3% even though the help centre advertises zero FX and deposit fees.
good_for: Heavy spenders outside the US who can use the US$2,000 monthly cashback cap on the Pro or Max tier (4.5%–6% paid in USDT)
Users who want to keep custody of their crypto until the moment of payment and fund the card from many chains
not_for: Anyone who wants a free card — every tier carries an issue fee and an annual fee
US citizens applying for the international card (excluded by the terms); US residents only via the separate US terms
Frequent cash withdrawals (up to US$2 + 3% per withdrawal, US$750/day)
watch_outs: Fee contradiction: help-centre pages say 'zero deposit fees and zero foreign exchange fees'; the Card Terms (effective 2025-10-31) disclose up to 3% FX + up to 1% international and up to 1% deposit — the terms are modelled.
Cashback is paid in periodic batches (FAQ: quarterly, up to 90 days), only while the membership is active, and spend above the monthly cap earns 0.5%–1%.
Spending is a credit line secured by your collateral; limits 'can be reduced to $0' at any time and collateral can be liquidated under the terms.
No official country list found; the app decides eligibility at sign-up ('over 200 supported regions').
Season 3 cashback rules have a start date (2026-06-01) but no end date — rates may change.
